profiles.latency-first: Prefer the viable topology with the lowest expected end-to-end input-to-display delay. Favor local rendering/native netplay or original LAN/System-Link over video streaming when a credible implementation exists. Mark predictions as candidates until measured in a real session.
profiles.easy-first: Prefer the smallest setup surface and fastest path to a playable session, even if it adds streaming encode/decode latency.
profiles.balanced: Prefer a well-supported topology with good expected latency without adding disproportionate setup complexity.
profiles.fallback: Use when the preferred topology fails compatibility, stability, reachability, or latency acceptance.

recommendation_policy.evidence_rule: Recommendation labels describe intent and expected topology. A route becomes proven only after an actual session records measured/observed results.

runtimes.notes: Desktop NetPlay supports local-multiplayer GameCube/Wii titles. Matching Dolphin versions and matching game region/revision are important; identical dumps are strongly recommended. Wii NetPlay is documented as more temperamental than GameCube NetPlay.

xemu supports NAT, UDP Tunnel, and Bridged Adapter networking. UDP Tunnel is intended for xemu-to-xemu Internet play; Bridged Adapter is useful with real Xbox hardware and XLink Kai. Virtual Xbox MAC addresses must be unique.

Preferred PS1 local-emulation runtime. Pair with Parsec for the easiest remote-couch setup or Sunshine + Moonlight when streaming remains desirable but latency is prioritized. For the lowest expected remote-play latency, compare against Mednafen native netplay rather than assuming any streaming path is optimal.

Primary PS1 latency-first candidate. Both players run matching local emulation/content and connect through a Mednafen netplay server, avoiding video encode/decode and remote video transport. Actual advantage depends on network conditions and synchronization behavior; validate with a real match. Mednafen uses save states for synchronization, so important memory-card state should be backed up or isolated.

Nostalgia v0.1 does not assume a universal PCSX2 native netplay layer. For local multiplayer titles, remote couch remains a practical route unless a lower-latency game-specific network recipe is validated.

RetroArch netplay requires matching RetroArch/core/content and a deterministic, sufficiently performant core. Current Libretro FAQ explicitly says the netplay model is unsuitable for PSX/N64/Dreamcast/GameCube/Wii/3DS-class systems; do not use RetroArch netplay as a PS1 latency fallback.
Flycast Dojo focuses on netplay/replay and documents P2P Match Codes, direct-IP play, and virtual-LAN options. Matching game files are required for netplay.

transports.notes: Easiest remote-couch transport. One player hosts the emulator and remote gamepads are exposed as virtual controllers. Good baseline, but the guest experiences network plus encode/decode/display latency.

Remote-couch option to evaluate when streaming is desired but latency matters more than setup simplicity. Sunshine is the host and Moonlight is the client. On Windows, full virtual gamepad support requires the documented virtual-input setup. Treat lower-latency claims as a candidate until measured on the players' hardware/network.
Used with games whose original console LAN/System-Link mode is verified by XLink Kai. With xemu, use the bridged-network path described by xemu/XLink documentation.

packs.use_for: GameCube/Wii local multiplayer transported through Dolphin NetPlay
Original Xbox System Link over Internet or mixed emulator/real-hardware sessions
Local multiplayer games where one authoritative emulator host is simplest

latency-first.reason: Both players render locally; removes streaming encode/decode and remote video delivery from the control loop.

balanced.reason: Keeps DuckStation's simple authoritative-host model while targeting a low-latency streaming stack.

easy-first.reason: Smallest setup surface and easiest controller passthrough.

packs.use_for: PS1 campaign that explicitly compares latency-first, balanced streaming, and easy-first paths and records which one actually wins on the players' network.
